title: The Summer of Port Alder Anew
premise: Marine biologist Xanthe Blackwood returns to the coastal town of Port Alder to run a sea turtle rehabilitation program, hiding from a scandal that cost her both her reputation and her engagement. When the town's centennial festival committee launches an anonymous pen-pal project meant to heal old community rifts, a clerical error pairs Xanthe with Dev Okafor, the harbor inspector whose testimony once destroyed her mentor — and who is now investigating her program's funding. Writing to 'Stranger A' and 'Stranger B,' they confess truths they'd never say face-to-face, even as their daytime rivalry sharpens into reluctant alliance over a poaching ring threatening the turtles. At the festival's lantern night, identities are revealed, Dev must choose between exposing Xanthe's falsified permit or shielding her, and Xanthe must choose between the career she rebuilt and the man who finally sees her whole. They choose each other, turning themselves in together and rebuilding the program on honest ground as Port Alder's found family closes ranks around them.
about_author: A. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who spent three summers counting sea turtle nests along the Pacific coast before trading field notebooks for fiction. Their romances are known for salt-stung settings, stubborn scientists, and communities that refuse to let anyone heal alone.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Feeling
chapters.summary: Xanthe arrives in Port Alder with two duffel bags and a rule: no attachments, only data. Her POV establishes the turtle rehab center, her self-imposed emotional discipline, and the town that remembers her mentor's fall. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Committee's Bright Idea
chapters.summary: Festival chair Rosa Aguilar announces the anonymous pen-pal project to mend decades of harbor feuds; participants draw numbers from a bait bucket. Xanthe signs up to appease Rosa, needing town goodwill for her grant renewal. Beat: reluctant hope, first glimpse of Dev arguing with Rosa about dock safety citations.

chapters.title: Stranger B Writes First
chapters.summary: Xanthe receives a blunt, funny letter criticizing the festival's plastic lanterns — signed Stranger B. She fires back a correction about biodegradable alternatives, delighted to spar with someone who can't see her flinch. Beat: unexpected spark through anonymity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sank a Mentor
chapters.summary: Dev Okafor's POV: he arrives to audit the rehab center's permits, carrying guilt over testimony that ended Dr. Voss's career years ago. He clashes with Xanthe on the dock over a citation. Beat: antagonism laced with unwanted attraction he refuses to name.

chapters.title: Dead Turtle at Mile Marker Nine
chapters.summary: A poached hawksbill washes ashore; Xanthe's necropsy reveals fishing-line wounds inconsistent with accidental bycatch. Dev, reluctantly drawn in, agrees to look the other way on paperwork while they investigate. Beat: enemies forced into uneasy partnership by shared purpose.

chapters.title: Letters We Shouldn't Send
chapters.summary: Alternating letters between Strangers A and B grow intimate — Xanthe confesses fear of being known; Dev admits he was pressured into his old testimony. Neither recognizes the other despite daily proximity. Beat: dramatic irony deepening, tenderness through paper.

chapters.title: Found Family, Salt-Flavored
chapters.summary: Rosa, teenage volunteer Priya, and retired fisherman Elio fold Xanthe into Sunday dinners and net-mending nights. She resists, then stays late helping Priya study for her marine science exam. Beat: walls cracking; belonging offered without conditions.

chapters.title: Permit Number 4471
chapters.summary: Dev discovers Xanthe renewed the center's permit using Voss's forged signature — her one dishonest act, done to save the turtles after funders fled. He says nothing, but pockets the document. Beat: moral vertigo; his silence becomes complicity.

chapters.title: Night Patrol
chapters.summary: Stakeout at the nesting beach catches poachers' boat lights; Xanthe and Dev hide in dune grass, pressed shoulder to shoulder, whispering a plan. Almost-kiss interrupted by a radio call. Beat: tension snapping toward intimacy.

chapters.title: The Letter That Names It
chapters.summary: Stranger B writes about falling for someone impossible — his audit target. Xanthe realizes with cold horror it could be her, and that she feels the same about someone she shouldn't. Beat: longing sharpened by dread.

chapters.title: Elio's Old Charts
chapters.summary: Elio produces decades-old charts showing a hidden cove used by the poaching ring since before Dev's time — implicating families Dev must now confront, including Rosa's nephew. Beat: justice gets complicated; loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Midsummer Gala, Unmasked Almost
chapters.summary: At the festival fundraiser, Xanthe and Dev dance; a drunk councilman nearly exposes the pen-pal mix-up, hinting the pairings were deliberately sabotaged by someone on the committee. Beat: romance blooming publicly, conspiracy seeded.

chapters.title: Priya Follows the Lights
chapters.summary: Priya secretly photographs the cove at night and is nearly caught; Xanthe rescues her, sustaining a gash. Dev bandages it, hands shaking. Beat: stakes turn physical; protectiveness becomes undeniable love.

chapters.title: What the Audit Demands
chapters.summary: Dev's supervisor demands the completed report including Permit 4471. Dev requests an extension, lying for the first time in his career. Beat: his integrity fracturing under the weight of what he wants and what's right.

chapters.title: Confession in the Hatchery
chapters.summary: Xanthe tells Dev everything — the forgery, the shame, why she counts turtles instead of heartbreaks. He almost tells her he knows; instead he kisses her. Beat: catharsis and surrender, happiness built on a hidden fault line.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Letter
chapters.summary: An unsigned letter to the festival committee accuses the rehab center of fraud and names the pen-pal pairings as rigged to force exactly this outcome. Suspicion falls on everyone; Rosa is devastated. Beat: trust collapsing town-wide.

chapters.title: Lantern Night Betrayal
chapters.summary: Dev's supervisor arrives unannounced during the lantern release, having obtained the permit file. Confronted before the crowd, Dev shields Xanthe by claiming he lost the document — perjury. Beat: climax begins; sacrifice mirroring sacrifice.

chapters.title: Stranger A, Revealed
chapters.summary: In the chaos, the pen-pal letters are read aloud by accident — Rosa realizes the clerical swap, and the whole town learns Strangers A and B are Xanthe and Dev. Public humiliation, private relief: they finally know each other completely. Beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Courtroom
chapters.summary: Rather than let Dev fall alone, Xanthe reports herself, and the pair present the poaching evidence to the state together, negotiating amnesty in exchange for the ring's prosecution. The town testifies on their behalf. Beat: truth as the only workable foundation.

chapters.title: Voss Returns
chapters.summary: Xanthe's disgraced mentor arrives uninvited, furious — then softens seeing the hatchery full and Priya teaching schoolchildren. Voss offers to co-sign a clean permit application. Beat: forgiveness across generations; the past released.

chapters.title: The Festival Ends, the Season Begins
chapters.summary: Final festival night: real biodegradable lanterns, Rosa's amended pen-pal reveal celebrated rather than shamed, Dev resigning his inspector post to co-direct the center. Nesting season peaks — a record hatch. Beat: full-circle joy, chosen family assembled.

chapters.title: A Heart, Trained at Last
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs: months later, Xanthe and Dev write each other signed letters anyway, keeping the ritual. On the beach at dawn she admits the heart is trainable after all — trained, like any muscle, by showing up daily. Beat: quiet, earned happily-ever-after.
